title: Overcoming strength-ductility tradeoff with high pressure thermal treatment

recollection.starting_material: Guess: The paper may have started with a medium-carbon steel or an aluminum alloy that commonly exhibits a strength-ductility tradeoff.
recollection.intervention: Guess: It likely employed a novel high-pressure heat-treatment process that altered the material's microstructure at elevated temperatures.
recollection.structure: Guess: The microstructure may have developed refined grains or formed precipitation phases that improved both strength and ductility.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The high-pressure environment could have accelerated diffusion and suppressed certain phase transformations, stabilizing a beneficial microstructure.
recollection.results: Guess: The authors might have reported a simultaneous increase in yield strength (by a few hundred MPa) and ductility (by several percentage points in elongation to failure).

score.note: The intervention merely restates the title’s high-pressure heat treatment and lacks the specific HPHT hexahedron-anvil method. The proposed grain refinement/precipitation structure and diffusion/phase-suppression mechanism do not match the coherent hierarchical FCC/B2 microstructure and dislocation-transfer mechanism. No actual values (1150 MPa fracture strength, 36% uniform elongation, nearly 100% enhancement) were recalled.
